key_insight: Raising the critical plasma spraying parameter (CPSP) improved the fracture toughness of atmospheric plasma-sprayed Al2O3 coatings, regardless of whether it was measured by Vickers indentation or SENB.
engineering_relevance: The results help process engineers tune plasma-spray conditions to obtain tougher ceramic coatings on titanium alloy substrates for wear- and damage-resistant applications.
method: Compared Al2O3 coatings deposited at different CPSP values using atmospheric plasma spraying.
Measured fracture toughness by Vickers indentation and single edge notched beam (SENB) testing.
Evaluated residual compressive stress and compared trends between the two toughness methods.
evidence_signal: As CPSP increased from 0.83 to 1.17, indentation-derived toughness rose from 1.81 ± 0.03 to 2.22 ± 0.02 MPa·m^1/2, while SENB-derived toughness increased from 0.89 ± 0.05 to 1.25 ± 0.02 MPa·m^1/2.
watch_item: Absolute fracture toughness values differed notably between indentation and SENB, so method selection and calibration matter when comparing coating performance.
paper_title: Comparative evaluation of mechanical properties in plasma-sprayed Al2O3 coatings via Vickers indentation and single edge notched beam methods
